profile.headline: Engineer, educator, and researcher working where business, engineering, and AI meet
profile.bio: I spent years as a high-tech engineer in advanced manufacturing before moving into business education. Today I teach business analytics and research methods, lead student capstone projects, and research how AI is reshaping business and engineering practice. I believe the hardest and most interesting problems now sit between disciplines.
profile.bio2: This site is my working window: experiential learning projects that give business students real work experience, ideas on teaching and learning, applied AI, and a running watch on the diamond and jewelry market.
profile.statement: These student projects from recent semesters are built on real-world data and live business scenarios, because business judgment grows from analyzing messy evidence and making real decisions, not from textbook cases. Several led to public presentations and showcases.

projects.title: Bridging the AI Skills Gap
projects.description: Two student teams compare what educators teach with what employers demand. Findings are headed to a conference.

projects.title: Amazon Marketplace Analysis
projects.description: Students analyze real Amazon listings in JMP Pro and decide whether a new seller could compete.

projects.title: The Full Research Cycle
projects.description: From literature review to peer review and a conference-style presentation.

projects.title: Bayes for Supplier Quality
projects.description: Conditional probability applied to supplier quality and supply-chain decisions.

news.title: Diamonds may not be forever, at least in value terms
How will AI transform the UK jewellery and gemstone industry?
Lab-grown wholesale prices down about 13% year over year in Q2
China produces over 60% of lab-grown diamonds; Shanghai exports up 65%
Lab-grown retail prices down about 88% since 2020
AI becoming core to jewellery manufacturing and retail

editions.comment: Natural stones carry a 26% per-carat premium for crossing the 1-carat mark. Lab-grown prices are tightly clustered, which points to formula-based retail pricing.
